units.passage: You may use AI as a tool, but you may not use AI to replace your own beautiful brain.
units.why: Birdsall: "You may use AI as a tool, but you may not use AI to replace your own beautiful brain": student stays the thinker, P32.

units.passage: Active engagement with course materials, critical thinking and judgment, and expression of original ideas should never be outsourced to technology.
units.why: Critical thinking and original ideas "should never be outsourced to technology": AI should not replace the student's thinking (P32). Final codes after reconciliation: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=should-not, policy_type=P32, unit_stance=restrict.

units.passage: Students must be the primary author of any submitted work.
units.why: "Students must be the primary author of any submitted work" keeps the student as principal thinker/author, P32.
units.fit_note: Speaks of authorship rather than problem solving.

units.passage: Our goal is to use AI as part of your overall skill building, not to replace your own work.
units.why: "not to replace your own work": AI is part of skill building but must not substitute the student's own thinking, matching P32.

units.passage: While the AI language models can help refine your writing, it is important to remember that it is an AI system and not a substitute for your critical thinking and creativity. If you choose to use this tool, apply it as a supplement to your writing process and not rely solely on its suggestions.
units.policy: In the example allowing statement, AI is not a substitute for the student's critical thinking and creativity; students apply it as a supplement to their writing process and do not rely solely on its suggestions.
units.why: The sample says AI is 'not a substitute for your critical thinking and creativity' and tells students to 'apply it as a supplement ... and not rely solely on its suggestions', so students stay the primary thinker (P32); it limits how far the permitted use may go, so the unit stance is restrict.

units.passage: Gen AI must not compromise the fundamental principles of human integrity, not technology, being at the center of all academic work to promote academic honesty and intellectual exchange.
units.why: The core principle that "human integrity, not technology, being at the center of all academic work" is a principle for AI use, so P32 (humans stay central) over P56 because it constrains how AI is used.
units.fit_note: An institutional principle that technology not displace human integrity, not specifically about students being the primary problem-solver.

units.passage: AI tools are intended to support, not replace, human judgment.
units.why: "AI tools are intended to support, not replace, human judgment" is a principle that AI should not take over thinking, P32.
units.fit_note: General principle about human judgment, not specifically student problem-solving.

units.passage: AI should not replace your individual effort or original work but rather, should be used as supplemental resources to support your own analysis, critical thinking, and problem-solving.
units.why: 'AI should not replace your individual effort or original work' keeps the student as the main worker, P32.

units.passage: AI should not replace your struggle and effort but rather, should be used to support your learning, and expand your analysis, critical thinking, problem-solving, and production.
units.why: 'AI should not replace your struggle and effort' keeps the student doing the work, P32.

units.passage: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool.
units.why: 'Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance' asks users to keep their own thinking central, so P32 with should (no 'must').
units.fit_note: Frames it as periodic self-evaluation, not only a rule about being the primary problem-solver.

units.passage: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning.
units.policy: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning.
units.why: 'a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning' says AI must not replace the user's own work, P32.

units.passage: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool.
units.why: 'prevent an overreliance on the tool' keeps the person as primary thinker, P32.
units.fit_note: Periodic self-evaluation duty.

units.passage: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool.
units.why: 'prevent an overreliance on the tool' is P32.
units.fit_note: Periodic self-evaluation duty.

units.passage: Not use AI tools to replace independent thinking, analysis or engagement with course content.
units.why: "Not use AI tools to replace independent thinking, analysis or engagement with course content" keeps the student as the primary thinker, P32.

units.passage: Always employ human judgment when using AI outputs and be aware of misuse or misapplication where human judgment is critical
units.why: "Always employ human judgment when using AI outputs" keeps people as the decision-makers, nearest P32; it is not limited to students solving problems.
units.fit_note: Applies to all users of AI output and not only to a student's problem-solving.
